newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fairyoung seen in port unit spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Fairyoung seen in port unit spinoff.

text.p: Fairyoung Holdings Ltd is seeking a separate listing for its port operations arm, Pacific Ports Co, by issuing 200 million new shares with dealing expected to start on April 25, market sources said on Thursday.

The shares would be offered in a range of between HK$2.60 and HK$3.24 per share with the final price to be fixed on April 11, the property investment and securities trading company told analysts in a presentation on Thursday.
It said about 160 million shares would be placed with institutions and professional investors, and 40 million shares offered in an initial public offering (IPO) from April 15 to 18.

Analysts said 10 percent of the IPO shares would be reserved for employee subscription and the company had also granted underwriters an overallotment option to require it to issue up to another 30 million new shares.
The proceeds raised from the new issue would be used to develop Fairyoung's existing ports in China, to invest in new ports and as working capital, analysts said.
Pacific Ports has stakes in four terminal projects in China's Xiamen, Nanjing and Suzhou, but Xiamen's Berth 12 was the only new terminal in operation, one analyst said.
"Its other port projects will gradually come on stream later this year," he said.
The company forecast net profit of not less than HK$50 million for the year ending December 31, 1997, after making a projected loss no greater than HK$17 million in 1996, another analyst said.

The analysts said they felt the price range of about 30 times prospective 1997 price earnings multipule looked a bit ambitious, while its 14-28 percent discount on net asset value was not as attractive as other infrastructure plays.
